memory-intro-stores.alt: Sights, sounds and touch enter sensory memory, which holds them for about half a second for sights and a few seconds for sounds; unattended input fades. Attention moves some of it into short-term memory, which holds a few items for about 20 to 30 seconds unless it is rehearsed; rehearsal keeps it active. Encoding moves information from short-term memory into long-term memory, which has a very large capacity and lasts from days to a lifetime; retrieval brings it back into short-term memory. A box below shows the working memory model of the short-term store: a central executive that directs attention, a phonological loop for words and sounds, and a visuospatial sketchpad for images and places.
